facts.statement: The species Xiphodolamia barbadica was described by Casier in 1958.
facts.quote: Xiphodolamia barbadica Casier 1958

facts.quote: Xiphodolamia serrata Adnet et al. 2009

facts.statement: Xiphodolamia is known only from isolated teeth found in Europe, Africa, and Asia.
facts.quote: It is only known from isolated teeth, but has been found in Europe, Africa, and Asia.

facts.statement: Xiphodolamia is assumed to have been a pelagic shark living in deeper waters, with fossils found in deposits like the London Clay and Eocene strata in Denmark.
facts.quote: It is assumed to be pelagic, occurring more frequently in deeper water deposits, most notably the London Clay and Eocene deposits in Denmark.

facts.statement: Xiphodolamia is distinguished by a rectangular tooth root and a twisted blade, a combination unique among mackerel sharks.
facts.quote: It is distinguished by its rectangular root and twisted blade, unique among mackerel sharks.

facts.statement: It is unclear what ecological niche the specialized dentition of Xiphodolamia helped the animal exploit.
facts.quote: It is unclear what niche this specialized dentition helped exploit.

facts.statement: The consensus classification places Xiphodolamia as an unusual member of the order Lamniformes.
facts.quote: it is now the consensus Xiphodolamia is an unusual member of the order Lamniformes.

facts.statement: The exact placement of Xiphodolamia within Lamniformes remains uncertain, particularly regarding its relationship to Lamnidae and Isurus.
facts.quote: However, its placement within Lamniformes is uncertain, especially its relationship to Lamnidae and Isurus.

facts.statement: Some researchers have placed Xiphodolamia in its own family, Xiphidolamnidae.
facts.quote: Some have placed it in its own family, Xiphidolamnidae.

facts.statement: Xiphodolamia serrata is a serrated variety known from the Upper Eocene of Africa and Arabia.
facts.quote: X. serrata is a serrated variety known from the Upper Eocene of Africa and Arabia.

facts.statement: The development of serrations in Xiphodolamia mirrors that of Otodus in the Ypresian, representing an example of convergent evolution.
facts.quote: The development of serrations in Xiphodolamia mirrors that of Otodus in the Ypresian, and thus is an example of convergent evolution.

facts.statement: Xiphodolamia fossils have been found in the Nanjemoy Formation in Maryland, the Santee Limestone in South Carolina, the Scotland Beds in Barbados, and New Jersey.
facts.quote: Maryland (Nanjemoy Formation) South Carolina (Santee Limestone) Barbados (Scotland Beds) New Jersey

facts.statement: Xiphodolamia fossils have been found in the London Clay in England, the Tielt Formation in Belgium, the Dongen Formation in the Netherlands, as well as in Italy, Romania, and Slovakia.
facts.quote: England (London Clay) Belgium (Tielt Formation) The Netherlands (Dongen Formation) Italy Romania Slovakia

facts.statement: Xiphodolamia fossils have been found in the Tologaysor Formation in Kazakhstan, as well as in Jordan, Iran, and the Soğucak Formation in Turkey.
facts.quote: Kazakhstan (Tologaysor Formation) Jordan Iran Turkey (Soğucak Formation)

facts.statement: Xiphodolamia lived from the Ypresian to the Messinian, spanning from 56 to 5.333 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Messinian (56 to 5.333 million years ago)
